correctness.rationale: The exact edge defect identity and two-case bounds were reconstructed algebraically. A smooth trial proves ne_n is bounded; minimizing transformed nodal functions are bounded in H1, have exact asymptotic L2 normalization, and meet antiperiodic trace conditions. Local same-sign bounds and weak lower semicontinuity, including treatment of the zero set, establish liminf ne_n >= 3pi^2/8. The transformed cosine recovery sequence has exactly normalized fourth moment and yields the matching limsup. Fourth-root expansion yields 3pi^2/16. The bipartite signed-cycle block representation is an ell_4-isometry. Code checks are only diagnostic and cannot replace the limit proof.

originality.rationale: Three materially relevant full-text primary articles were compared at the level of matrix, scalar field, norm, all-parameter quantifiers, and limit. Their exact signed-cycle formulas determine quadratic or Hermitian spectra, not the induced real ell_4 norm. A separate same-dimension ell_4 two-coordinate norm and unsigned harmonic cycle results do not imply the n-to-infinity signed-cycle constant. No covering result was identified in the actual published-record searches or local claim ledgers. Residual bibliographic uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed pre-2015 work on induced norms of skew-circulants or asymptotic antiperiodic shifts might imply this leading coefficient; no decisive such source was identified.
The search is bounded, not a universal novelty certificate; no independent external review has occurred.

value.rationale: The all-size leading-order induced real ell_4 norm deficit is a natural quantitative invariant of a frustrated sparse graph operator. It is not a dimension-specific table entry: the proof explains why the first nonzero cost has order n^-2 and determines its sharp coefficient. The coefficient differs from the Hilbert spectral deficit and arises from a nontrivial nonlinear variable transformation, compactness, and sharp continuum Poincare limit. It is useful as an exact benchmark for stability of sign-frustrated averaging on non-Hilbert sequence spaces, independently of a downstream theorem.
